verdict.rationale: Name.com offers its own bulk capabilities: the API's availability check accepts up to 50 domains per call, the site offers Bulk Domain Search, and a community user reports selecting 50 domains at once to change nameservers. API endpoints for writes such as registration, DNS records and transfers are documented only per item, so bulk mutation for programmatic or agent workflows is unproven. missing for 10: documented bulk/batch write endpoints in the API (bulk DNS, renewals, settings changes), first-party docs for UI bulk management, recent independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can perform bulk operations across many items at once

citations.quote: Checks whether up to 50 domain names are purchasable and returns **discovery** pricing for each result.
browsing expiring domains, premium names, and bulk search options.
They have a very convenient way to do bulk changes, so you can select 50 domains at once, and tell name.com to change all of them to your name servers.
